correctness.rationale: Complete proof for arbitrary finite simple loopless digraphs: external SCC arcs yield an invariant join-simplex contraction; otherwise open hemispheres on the SCC zero-sum representation cover precisely because each SCC is strongly connected, with nerve exactly the acyclic-arc complex. Every nonempty intersection is a strict invariant convex cone on which every setwise stabilizer subgroup has a fixed point and equivariant radial contraction. Genuine equivariant nerve comparison gives all subgroup fixed spaces. The explicit complete-case fixed-dimension formula follows from signed orbit stabilizers and a zero-sum constraint. Arrow reversal is antipodal and its quotient is real projective. The two included checkers independently tested 93 complete-graph subgroup cases and 491 general directed-graph/symmetry pairs. Those finite tests alone would not prove the theorem.

originality.rationale: The same ordinary acyclic-arc complex and sphere/contractible dichotomy were established by Hultman; the complete-case ordinary sphere and open hemisphere nerve were established earlier. The new claim is a signed-graph-automorphism genuine equivariant dichotomy for arbitrary directed graphs, including all subgroup-fixed spaces and a projective-space arrow-reversal quotient. The inspected published results state nonequivariant equivalences, which cannot alone imply the fixed and quotient claims. Dedicated published-finding corpus and own-ledger searches found no implication covering this exact signed equivariant statement; the uninspected 1999 full article is a stated remaining priority risk.
residual_risks: The 1999 Björner–Welker full text could not be inspected; its abstract does not resolve whether a strengthening is discussed in the body.
An older unindexed equivariant-order-poset theorem could cover a subcase; priority should be independently assessed.
A full genuine equivariant good-cover nerve lemma is used, with its special stabilizer-fixed hypotheses verified in the proof.

value.rationale: The natural class of all finite directed acyclic-arc-subset complexes admits a uniform model that determines actual geometric fixed spaces under every signed symmetry, not just an Euler characteristic or character. The derived complete-case projective quotient gives unbounded-dimensional families with integral 2-torsion even though the ambient complex is spherical. The distinction matters for symmetry quotients and equivariant topology; the result is not a numerical increment or an isolated small invariant.
